text.tspan: From Seeing to Touching: Turning Everyday
Object Encounters into Situated Braille Learning Moments
Visually impaired people encounter countless everyday objects, yet these
moments rarely turn into intentional learning opportunities. We explore how
to transform natural object encounters into situated braille learning moments

svg.text: From Semantic Access to Literacy Access

text.tspan: Understanding what an object is, its function,
Connecting the object to its written form

svg.text: FST: From Everyday Object Encounters to Situated Braille Learning Moments

text.tspan: FST turns everyday object encounters into situated braille learning moments
by bridging semantic access through speech and literacy access through touch.
I see eggs, milk, an apple,
CABLE is a modular pipeline that connects AI glasses, an interaction-coordinating agent,
braille translation, and an electroosmotic tactile display to deliver situated braille learning.

svg.text: Provide visual, auditory, and haptic cues
The agent does not directly control the EOP actuators. All tactile output is produced only through the braille pipeline and display driver.

text.tspan: An end-to-end system integrating AI glasses,
dialogue agent, braille pipeline, and electroosmotic
A systematic analysis of design choices,

svg.text: How accurately are relevant objects detected?
How effectively does the agent confirm user intent?
How correct and timely is the braille translation?
How well can users perceive and learn from the tactile output?
How does repeated exposure affect short- and long-term learning?

text.tspan: Everyday objects can be powerful entry points for braille learning. We
will conduct user studies with visually impaired learners and explore
richer interaction strategies and real-world deployments.
